name: Reconcile the access review population to authoritative identity sources
description: Build the review population by reconciling the identity provider, the HR system, and each in-scope application, and record the reconciliation so completeness is demonstrable rather than assumed.

steps.action: Enumerate every in-scope system holding entitlements, working from the declared system boundary rather than from memory.
Identify the authoritative source for each identity class: employees, contractors, service accounts, shared accounts, and privileged roles.
Extract entitlements per system and reconcile against those sources, documenting and explaining every difference.
Assign a named human owner to every service account and shared account so the review has an accountable reviewer.
Record the population generation method — system, query, date, and filters — as a standing part of the review record.
Re-run the reconciliation each cycle so newly added systems enter the population automatically.

implementation_considerations: Reconciliation is only meaningful against a current system boundary. If the boundary is stale, fix it first.
Assigning human owners to service accounts is usually the slowest step and is best done incrementally by risk.
typical_duration: One cycle to build the reconciliation, thereafter incremental.
prerequisites: Read access to entitlement data in each in-scope system

verification_method.how: Independently re-derive the population from the authoritative sources and confirm it matches the reviewed population, with all differences explained.

residual_risk_note: Newly onboarded systems remain the recurring source of population drift; without a link from system onboarding to review scope, the gap reopens.
period_limitation_note: A reconstructed population does not retroactively make an earlier review complete. Reviews performed during the period over an incomplete population remain incomplete.
notes: Backfilled with responsible_role and implementation_considerations in the CC6 phase (schema 0.2.0).
